summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1b in Infectum-wa (JTM 2.12/5)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr saymiwo ste maye, u ṣoṣ diḏe, maye d baḏənǧan, salča, bam maye šaḥine, maḥtiwo aʕle, maṭəfiwo aʕle w mbašliwole.
data.translation: Danach machten sie noch die Sauce dafür, Tomatenmark, d.h. sālča in heißem Wasser (aufgelöst), das gaben sie darüber, bedeckten es damit und kochten es.

rationale: New Infectum-wa box and same construction with understood sauce.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.27/1293)

data.turoyo: <...> I rawmo ṭayəfo wa w zayədo wa w qaləbo wa ʕal an arġalyoṯanək. <...>
data.translation: <...> The pond had overflowed and had risen and had spilled over into those rain channels. <...>

rationale: First I Preterit-wa box: transparent ṭayəfo plus separately written wa, with pond subject and coordinated state/event predicates. English is the supplied project machine translation [MT]; sense determined from Turoyo.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.20/3816)

data.translation: <...> The water used to overflow there. <...>

rationale: New I Preterit-wa box, plural ṭayfiwo corresponding to the a-vocalism of ṭayəf; recurrent rainfall context retained as aspect evidence, classification provisional. English is the supplied project machine translation [MT]; sense determined from Turoyo.

summary: New sense 1b: (mit ʕal) Flüssigkeit über etw. giessen, etw. überfluten;

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: (mit ʕal) Flüssigkeit über etw. giessen, etw. überfluten;

rationale: Two cooking contexts put food in an ʕal target phrase; the liquid is expressed as maye or supplied by the sauce context. The construction differs from causing a vessel to overflow. Full submersion is not built into the gloss.

data.turoyo: A ṭlawḥe səmoqe, hanək ste, kmašəġatte, šafiro, bəṯr kmaṭifət aʕlayye maye
data.translation: Die roten Linsen, die wäschst du sorgfältig, dann bedeckst du sie mit Wasser

rationale: New construction in Infectum; explicit water and lentil target, without the unnecessary quantity false start.

summary: The new culinary frame is supported in two JTM recipes: explicit maye with plural ʕal target and understood sauce with singular ʕal target. The German recasts the food as the object of covering; the analysis follows the Turoyo liquid/target structure.
III maṭifət/maṭəfiwo is assigned to ṭyf rather than ṭfy from the vowel shape and liquid-application context; the identification remains open to native confirmation. Extinguishing is not established.
No vessel overflowing is mentioned in either cooking context, and no lid or solid cover is expressed. The gloss avoids asserting either complete submersion or a general non-liquid covering sense.
I at PrS 5/17 retains a basin subject and silver/gold contents, paralleling the existing I.1 example; the differently numbered match is not reprinted.
Round 2 is based on the supplied Jan Turoyo; accompanying English is project machine translation [MT]. Round 1 was read first and its proposals are not duplicated.
Jan supplies I Preterit-wa from uncontracted feminine ṭayəfo wa (Jan 1.27/1293). The same line repeats it after perception; the repetition is decided separately and quoted once.
Plural Ṭayfiwo am maye (Jan 2.20/3816) is provisionally placed with that a-vocalism series. Its habitual setting does not itself demand Infectum-wa; the box choice follows the form comparison.
Pond as container-subject and water as liquid-subject both remain inherited overflow sense 1. No new idiom, valency distinction or Detransitive follows from that participant difference.
No Jan III occurrence adds to or overturns round 1 liquid-pouring subsense 1b.
Do kmaṭifət/maṭəfiwo entail flooding or submerging, merely pouring over, or making the food float? The proposed gloss leaves degree of coverage open.
Confirm ṭyf versus ṭfy in the cooking forms; context favors liquid application and does not establish extinguishing.
Check supplied PrS 5/17 against inherited prs 12/24 before changing the existing basin quotation reference.
Confirm plural Ṭayfiwo as Preterit-wa alongside ṭayəfo wa, rather than a dialectal Infectum-wa with altered vocalism (Jan 2.20/3816).
Do separately written wa predicates at Jan 1.27/1293 describe a prior overflow result or a background state at the time of seeing? Keep the morphology separate from the English anterior wording.
